Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

mzLibR 0.1.0 (unreleased)

The first release. Versions follow each wire verb’s since.mzlibr in the bridge’s verb specs, which every help page’s Since section renders.

This release projects mzLib 1.0.596. The verbs marked needs the pyMzLib 0.2.0 bridge, needs the pyMzLib 0.3.0 bridge, needs the pyMzLib 0.4.0 bridge or needs the pyMzLib 0.6.0 bridge below are new in the bridge that release publishes; with an older bridge they are refused, naming the release they need. mzlibr_install_bridge() installs the bridge pyMzLib 0.7.0 publishes (mzLib 1.0.596, cc67b7a2), verified against that release’s SHA256SUMS.

mzLib 1.0.596 (the pyMzLib 0.7.0 bridge)

mzlibr_install_bridge() now installs the pyMzLib 0.7.0 bridge, built from mzLib 1.0.596 (tag commit cc67b7a2), up from 1.0.595. Several existing functions give a different answer, most because mzLib changed them; each is listed below, as pyMzLib 0.7.0’s upgrading notes list them. Every recording the help pages and articles replay was re-recorded from the 0.7.0 bridge (pyMzLib’s, byte for byte), and the live tests hold each to what that bridge returns.

The 0.7.0 bridge also has four verbs and three options this package does not project yet: genes map-residues (pyMzLib’s proteins.map_residues()), library calibrate-rt, stats fit-latent-mixed and stats fit-link; and ptmqtl pairs’ include_bounds and run_covariate and ptmqtl trait-effects’ scale = "log2_odds". docs/name-parity.md lists them as not yet ported. The fields they report on every call are projected now (below).

Calls that used to fail now succeed.

  • sdrf_isobaric_design() on a TMT10 SDRF that names its last channel TMT131 (mzLib #1467). PRIDE spells TMT10’s last channel TMT131, and it was refused as not a channel of TMT10. It now reads as channel 131N. TMT131 is still refused for TMT11, where 131N and 131C are both channels.
  • sdrf_design() on an SDRF with a missing replicate or a numbering gap (mzLib #1426). A biological replicate of not available, or no replicate column at all, was refused; mzLib now adds a number after the highest one the condition uses, and says so in notes. A gap in the fraction or technical replicate numbers is noted instead of refused.
  • A peptidoform_convert() batch with two modifications on one residue (mzLib #1457). One such line, for example PEPM[A][B]TIDE, failed the whole call with an mzlib_bridge_error (ArgumentException). Now only that line fails (below), and the rest of the batch converts.

Calls that used to succeed are now refused.

  • Malformed modification text in peptidoform_convert() (mzLib #1457), with source = "mzLib" (the default) or "MassShift". An empty modification (PEP[]TIDE), a modification that does not follow an unmodified residue (two leading groups, or two on one residue) and anything after the C-terminal modification were converted with a modification lost or moved. Each is now a "failed" row with failure_reason "UnknownFormat". An ambiguous MetaMorpheus sequence (|-joined candidates) still converts with a warning, unless a candidate ends in a C-terminal modification or the next one’s N-terminal modification lands on an already modified residue.

Same failure, different error.

  • A .parquet another process holds, or that you may not read (mzLib #1478). Every reader raised an mzlib_usage_error (Parquet file type not supported). It now raises an mzlib_bridge_error naming the I/O failure (IOException or UnauthorizedAccessException). A file that is not Parquet at all is still the usage error.

Same file, different value.

  • sdrf_design() keeps the SDRF’s biological replicate numbers (mzLib #1426). It used to rank them within each condition, so an SDRF that numbers a condition’s samples 22, 23, 24 gave 0, 1, 2. It now gives 21, 22, 23 (0-based), gaps included, because replicate 4 of one condition can be the same subject as replicate 4 of another, and a gap can be a lost sample. notes flags each condition whose numbers are not 1..N, where it used to list the renumbering, and the result carries a seventh caveat saying so. A design written with out carries those numbers too; MetaMorpheus refuses one with gaps until a release carries smith-chem-wisc/MetaMorpheus#2928.
  • diff_design() numbers contrast ids once over the whole analysis (mzLib #1476). With strata, c1 used to be each stratum’s own first comparison; it is now one comparison in every stratum, and a stratum that cannot run it skips the id. A stratum’s not_run lists the skipped contrast under its own label (condition=B vs condition=A, where it said condition (one level: A)) and gains an id column, NA when no default contrast stands for the entry. Two caveats are reworded to say so. Designs without strata are unchanged.
  • ptmqtl_occupancy() reports more "not_detected" cells (mzLib #1468). mzLib now defines not_detected as a covered-zero: peptidoforms covering the site were identified in the run and none carried the modification. The covering forms no longer have to be quantified, so a site covered only by unquantified forms gets a row it did not get before. fraction stays NA.
  • ptmqtl_occupancy() gains two columns, and out writes them: covering_peptidoforms and modified_peptidoforms, after unmodified_quantified (mzLib #1468), the k of n of each cell, counting identifications rather than intensity. Read a written table by header name, not by position; ptmqtl_trait_effects() reads both the old and the new layout. A new caveat says what the counts are. The shipped extdata/ptmqtl/trait_occupancy.tsv is the new layout.
  • ptmqtl_pairs(type = "covarying") reports exclude_ceiling NA when you do not pass keep_ceiling = TRUE, where it reported TRUE. mzLib made the option nullable and decides it inside PtmPairEngine.CoVarying (mzLib #1468); mzLibR does not restate mzLib’s rule to name the value. The pairs themselves are unchanged: ceilings are still left out by default.
  • ptmqtl_pairs() says why a co-varying pair was not tested, in a new test_status column ("tested", "not_estimable", "too_few_shared_runs", "both_sites_mostly_bounds"; NA for physical pairs), beside bounds_included and run_covariate_removed. The result gains include_bounds, min_untied_share, run_covariate_file, run_covariate_name and run_covariate_runs_missing, mzLib’s echo of the two options not yet projected. Its caveat now counts untested pairs by reason (“N co-varying pairs were not tested (…)”), where it said “N co-varying pairs are not_estimable”. spearman_method is still "not_estimable" for every untested pair.
  • ptmqtl_trait_effects() reports its scale (mzLib #1464), "natural_log_odds" at mzLib’s default, the unit of every effect, standard error and variance; a seventh caveat names it. The numbers are unchanged.
  • isobaric_kits() gains an sdrf_label column (mzLib #1467): each channel’s SDRF comment[label] by mzLib’s SdrfIsobaricLabels, such as TMT127N, ITRAQ114, DiLeu115a, and TMT131 for TMT10’s 131N. A sixth caveat says what the label is.
  • ProForma and Unimod output for a terminal modification that shares its name (mzLib #1442). Entries such as Methyl on X and Less Common:Methylation on X exist once for a side chain and once for a terminus. The terminal one now resolves, so peptidoform_convert(..., target = "ProForma") and target = "Unimod", and readers_read_records()’s pro_forma column, write its UNIMOD: accession where they wrote its typed name or left it unresolved.
  • peptidoform_fragments() gives a peptide with a permanently charged modification a mass one proton lower per charge. The bridge now takes UniProt’s modifications from mzLib’s own corrected list (Mods.UniprotModifications), as MetaMorpheus does. Trimethyllysine counts as C3H6, 42.046951 Da (Unimod’s Trimethyl), not UniProt’s charged 43.054227; the other modifications PSI-MOD marks charged move the same way (trimethylalanine, dimethylproline, O-(2-cholinephosphoryl)serine). This changes monoisotopic_mass, the modifications table’s mass and every fragment’s neutral_mass that includes it. peptide_mz() is unchanged, because fixed_charges drops from 1 to 0 at the same time. N,N,N-trimethylglycine is the exception: it stays at UniProt’s mass, one hydrogen heavy, until the bridge builds from an mzLib that includes mzLib #1415.
  • fixed_charges (in peptides) and formal_charge (in modifications) are deprecated and always 0. No peptide carries a charge on top of its mass any more; both columns stay until the bridge’s next protocol version removes them. ?peptide_mz and ?peptidoform_fragments say so, and a fragment’s m/z at charge z is now simply (neutral_mass + z * 1.00727646677) / z.

Statistics, designs and PTM-QTL (the pyMzLib 0.6.0 bridge)

Ported from pyMzLib 0.6.0, verb for verb; each needs the pyMzLib 0.6.0 bridge. Every number is mzLib’s, and every recording the help pages and articles replay is pyMzLib’s, byte for byte. New articles: vignette("diff") and vignette("ptmqtl"); the differential-abundance article gains a section for each new statistic.

  • stats_fit(contrasts = ): any comparison, with a confidence interval (mzLib #1452, EmpiricalBayes.ModerateContrasts). Give the contrasts file diff_design(out = ) writes beside the design (contrasts_<i>.tsv), or your own: a contrast id column, then exactly the design’s coefficient columns, one weight each. Each contrast is moderated with the same prior as the coefficients, has its own Benjamini-Hochberg family, and carries confidence_low and confidence_high, as limma’s contrasts.fit(), eBayes() and topTable(confint = ). The answers are a second table, fit$contrasts (an mzlibr_moderated_contrasts with confidence_level, tested_contrasts, weights and records), so the coefficient table is unchanged; coefficients may now be empty and defaults to character(0). confidence sets the level, as a fraction; left NULL, it is mzLib’s default (0.95). fit$contrasts_file names the file.
  • stats_fit(estimator = ): mzLib’s marginal-likelihood variance prior (mzLib #1368). "marginal_likelihood" fits the prior with each feature’s own residual df, so the unequal df that missing values cause are handled exactly; "moments_legacy" (limma’s eBayes(legacy = TRUE)) stays mzLib’s default, and the new fit$prior$estimator reports which was used. On the MALAT1 dilution series it lowers the prior df from 19.6 to 11.0 and drops the false FLuc call at half load.
  • An older bridge is named, not trusted. A bridge before pyMzLib 0.6.0 lists stats fit but ignores --contrasts and --estimator; stats_fit() then raises an mzlib_usage_error naming the 0.6.0 bridge instead of returning a fit that did not do what was asked.
  • stats_fit()’s caveats name the variance-prior estimator. The first caveat now begins moments_legacy: (or marginal_likelihood:), the residual_df_differ caveat names estimator = "marginal_likelihood", and the bh_adjusted caveat says “per coefficient and per contrast”. Every number is unchanged; only code that matches caveat text needs a look. On fewer than 3 features prior$scale is NA and prior$df 0 (mzLib #1398); ?stats_fit now says bridges before pyMzLib 0.6.0, not 0.5.1, reported the first feature’s variance there.
  • stats_combine_p(): one p-value per feature from several independent studies, by Fisher’s method or Stouffer’s, weighted or not (mzLib #1367, PValueCombination). method is required. Give each test’s effect and every p-value is read as two-sided and converted to the one-sided p-value for effect > 0 first, so opposite effects cancel. The tests hold the recordings to R’s pchisq() and qnorm(), recorded and computed here.
  • stats_correlate(): Spearman’s rho of every feature with a per-sample trait, optionally partial given covariates (given; mzLib #1367, #1446, SpearmanCorrelation). Each row carries rho, a two-sided p-value, the samples used and how the p-value was computed ("exact", "asymptotic" or "not_estimable", with rho and p NA). The tests hold every recorded row to stats::cor.test() run here.
  • stats_fit_logistic(): a logistic regression per feature of a 0/1 table, as R’s glm(family = binomial) (mzLib #1367): is a feature’s detection related to the condition? A feature the design separates is "separated", with NA statistics, instead of R’s huge coefficient. max_iterations and tolerance are mzLib’s when left NULL. The tests hold the recording to R 4.6.1’s glm() output and to glm.fit() run here.
  • stats_fit_mixed(): a linear mixed model per feature with a random intercept per group of samples, as nlme::lme(random = ~ 1 | group) (mzLib #1367), tested by Wald t on nlme’s containment df. estimator = "reml" or "ml"; left NULL, mzLib’s default (REML), which the result reports. The tests hold the recordings to nlme 3.1.169’s output and to nlme::lme() run here.
  • stats_entrapment_fdp(): the lower bound, combined and paired estimates of a search’s false discovery proportion at each q-value threshold (mzLib #1385, Wen et al. 2025, as FDRBench). ratio is required; paired is reported only at a ratio of exactly 1; thresholds left NULL is mzLib’s default sweep, 0.001 to 0.100.
  • diff_design(), with factor_spec() and covariate_spec(): a sample sheet to mzLib’s design matrix per stratum (mzLib #1450, AnalysisDesign), equal to R’s model.matrix() (the tests run it here), with its rank, aliased terms, warnings and the contrasts it cannot run; one row per default contrast with mzLib’s verdict on whether these samples can estimate it at all. Each stratum’s matrix is an R matrix named by sample id, and strata is a list named by stratum key. With out it writes design_<i>.tsv and contrasts_<i>.tsv, which stats_fit() reads.
  • diff_observations(): every peptide in every biological sample from a FlashLFQ or MetaMorpheus peptide table (mzLib #1455): log2 intensity, fractions summed and technical replicates averaged, or NA, never 0, with the reason in state. runs is a data.frame of file and sample, and optionally fraction and technical_replicate; basis has no default. mzLib’s shared-peptide normalization is always measured and reported, and subtracted with normalize = TRUE. responses_out writes the table stats_fit() reads.
  • ptmqtl_occupancy(), ptmqtl_pairs() and ptmqtl_trait_effects(): PTM site occupancy per run with each cell’s state (a censored cell has no fraction, never a 0), physical and co-varying PTM pairs (type is required; remove_run_level takes out a batch shift), and a per-run trait’s effect on logit occupancy with a random intercept per biological replicate (mzLib #1369, #1430, #1446). Positions are 1-based, unlike readers_read_occupancy().
  • The vendored specs are re-synced from bridge 60b1d259. scripts/sync-specs.R now reads a bare y or n in a spec as the string the bridge’s own YAML reader takes it for, where R’s yaml package read it as a boolean (stats correlate‘s and ptmqtl pairs’ n column).

Data: checksums, alignment, orthology, spectral libraries and SDRF scoping (the pyMzLib 0.6.0 bridge)

Ported from pyMzLib 0.6.0, verb for verb; each needs the pyMzLib 0.6.0 bridge and is refused, naming that release, by an older one. Every option left out is not sent, so mzLib’s default applies and the result says what was used. Every recording the help pages and articles replay is pyMzLib’s, byte for byte. A new article, vignette("library"); the PRIDE, protein-database and SDRF articles gain a section for each new verb.

  • pride_file_checksums(): the MD5 and exact size PRIDE recorded for each deposited file (mzLib #1427, wire pride checksums). A data.frame of file_name, md5, size_bytes and project_accession, its row names the file names, so checksums["README.txt", ] looks a file up by the name it was downloaded under. size_bytes is the exact download length, which neither other listing gives (PXD000001’s .xml.gz: 10,668,000 bytes, where pride_list_files() says 10,677,205), and md5 is not the manifest’s checksum (a SHA-1 where present). It is a third list: PRIDE’s generated/ files have no row. Zero rows is an answer; an unknown accession, or a project not yet published, raises mzlib_project_not_found; a list mzLib cannot read stays an mzlib_bridge_error (MzLibException). No timeout of mzLibR’s own. pride_download() and pride_download_files() still check no bytes, and now say so; the PRIDE article shows the check with file.size() and tools::md5sum().
  • proteins_align(): map a residue onto an isoform, an ortholog or another release (mzLib #1428, wire proteins align). A global affine alignment scored with BLOSUM62, for a list of c(source, target) pairs in one bridge call: records (one row per pair: score in half-bits, identical and substituted residues, residues facing a gap, the aligned rows) and residue_map (one row per residue, its counterpart’s position and letter, NA facing a gap, never the nearest residue). pair_index is 1-based. proteins_map_source_to_target() and proteins_map_target_to_source() look positions up, and proteins_alignments() splits a result into one alignment per pair. gap_open, gap_extend, end_gaps and max_cells default to NULL, mzLib’s (11, 1, "free", 200,000,000); residue_map = FALSE sends --no-residue-map. One pair is proteins_align(list(c(source, target))), as the spec spells it: there is no separate one-pair function, which is pyMzLib’s proteins.align().
  • proteins_parse_accessions(): entry, isoform or version, and applied variants (mzLib #1382, wire proteins parse-accession). P04637-2_S70N is entry P04637, isoform 2, with S70N; NP_000537.3_R72P is RefSeq NP_000537, version 3. It parses and never repairs: a FASTA header, a DECOY_ prefix, a |-joined group or mzLib’s P04637_2 collision counter is unrecognized and kept verbatim, and every accession is sent exactly as given, not trimmed.
  • proteins_build_orthology(): an Ensembl Compara orthology snapshot (mzLib #1381, wire genes orthology). From each species’ GTF (or gene table), every species’ homology dump - mzLib refuses a call without one - and the gene-tree file, all local; gtfs and gene_sets are named character vectors, production name to path. It reports what went in (gene_sets, gene_trees, dumps), the relationships per species pair (pairs; proteins_orthology_pair() finds one in either order), a snapshot_id to record with any result, with pair_status every gene’s status in one other species (has_ortholog, no_edge_in_shared_tree, tree_lacks_target_species, not_in_any_tree), and with out the Parquet snapshot it wrote (written). mzLibR reads no Parquet; the proteins article queries it with arrow. mzLib’s three-species test world is copied into tests/orthology/, kept byte-exact by .gitattributes because the recordings’ sha256s are over its bytes.
  • library_read() and library_read_many(): mzLib’s .msl spectral libraries (wire library read). One row per precursor, or per fragment ion with fragments = TRUE, in the library’s stored order; retention_time_unit is per row (iRT or minutes, never converted), and mzLib’s “not available” values (ion mobility 0.0, a NaN q-value, NCE 0, an empty protein) are NA. precursor_index is 1-based. index_only_threshold defaults to NULL, mzLib’s 1 GiB; limit and offset count precursors. The many-libraries form returns one long table and a files data.frame, in one bridge call.
  • sdrf_isobaric_design(): a TMT, TMTpro, iTRAQ or DiLeu design from an SDRF (wire sdrf isobaric-design). One row per file and annotated channel, or every reason there is none. It guesses neither the kit nor the plex: declare exactly one of plex_column, plex_file_name_pattern and single_plex. Its numbers are 1-based, as the SDRF writes them, where sdrf_design()’s are 0-based; the split is mzLib’s, and mzLibR converts neither. out names a folder for MetaMorpheus’s TmtDesign.txt.
  • sdrf_restrict(): an SDRF cut to the files one search read (wire sdrf restrict). mzLib joins X-calib.mzML to the row naming X.raw by stem, adds comment[searched data file], and reports what it could not place (searched_without_row, dropped_data_files, ambiguous, shared_stem). Name an element of searched_files by its acquired file to override the suffix rule. The result is an mzlibr_sdrf; sdrf_searched_data_files() reads the new column. Restrict first, then read a design: both design readers key on that column.

Same file, different value.

  • sdrf_pool(out = )’s written$path names the file mzLib wrote. mzLib adds .sdrf.tsv to a name that does not already end in it, so out = "x.tsv" writes x.tsv.sdrf.tsv. With the pyMzLib 0.6.0 bridge written$path says x.tsv.sdrf.tsv; older bridges reported x.tsv, a file that does not exist. The file written is the same, and an out already ending in .sdrf.tsv is unchanged. sdrf_restrict(out = ) reports its file the same way.

For contributors. The replay bridge (R/replay.R) gains pyMzLib 0.6.0’s rules for these verbs: a recording answers only a call with the same pairs, accessions, searched files or species on stdin, the same --sequences, --no-residue-map, --pair-status and --restrict-gene-trees choice, and the options it was recorded with; and, as in pyMzLib, a recording whose echo of an option is null never answers a call that sends it. The test harness gains recorded_bridge_call(), which runs a public function through the real transport and verb check against a recording and returns what it sent.

Defaults come from mzLib (the pyMzLib 0.5.0 bridge)

  • peptidoform_fragments() takes its defaults from mzLib, so a call that names no protease or dissociation type gives different peptides and ions. Every digestion argument (protease, dissociation, missed_cleavages, min_length, max_length, max_modifications, max_isoforms, terminus) now defaults to NULL, mzLibR sends nothing for it, and mzLib’s DigestionParams default applies. Two of the old defaults were mzLibR’s own and change:
    • protease: mzLib’s default is "trypsin", which also cuts before proline. The old default was "trypsin|P", which does not. Albumin’s default digest goes from 303 to 310 peptidoforms, and from 195 to 202 distinct sequences.
    • dissociation: mzLib names no default, so the bridge uses HCD (b and y ions) until it does (smith-chem-wisc/mzLib#1488). The old default was ETD (c and z-dot ions).
    The other defaults (missed cleavages, the length window, the modification and isoform caps, terminus) have the same values as before, now set by mzLib. To get the old answer, pass protease = "trypsin|P", dissociation = "ETD". A digest records min_length, max_length and missed_cleavages as NA when they were left to mzLib, since the bridge does not report those three back, and prints them as mzLib’s default. A max_length below min_length is refused only when both are given. The help page’s counts are re-measured at mzLib d10017ce.
  • pride_list_files() and pride_search() leave the page size to mzLib. page_size now defaults to NULL and is sent only when given, so mzLib’s own paging default applies (100 today, as before). The results never depended on it. A given page size is checked as before.
  • pride_list_files(), pride_list_ftp_files() and pride_search() add no timeout of their own. They defaulted to timeout = 300, which turned a PRIDE outage that hangs into an mzlib_timeout. mzLib already bounds each request (#1412: three retries after 5, 20 and 60 s, each attempt up to 100 s), so they now default to NULL and a hang is reported as mzlib_service_unavailable, after about 8 minutes per request. Pass timeout = 300 for the old limit; a number still cuts the call off with mzlib_timeout. The PRIDE article’s outage handling now waits minutes and tries once more, since mzLib has already retried, and ?mzlib_error says so.
  • ?stats_fit no longer says the bridge’s spline default is 4. With trend = TRUE and no spline_basis, mzLibR has always sent none; the 0.5.0 bridge now asks mzLib for none either, so mzLib sizes the trend as limma does and a trend fit on fewer than 30 features gets limma’s numbers. prior$spline_basis_count says what was used.
  • The help pages are re-rendered from the bridge’s specs, re-checked against mzLib d10017ce. PXD000001’s REST manifest listed 9 of the 14 files in its FTP tree on 2026-10-21, and ?pride_list_files says so rather than 8 of 13.

mzLib 1.0.595

Built from mzLib 1.0.595 (tag commit d10017ce), which carries mzLib 1.0.594 as well.

  • DIA-NN 2.x’s report.parquet reads (mzLib #1384, file type DiaNnReportParquet). DIA-NN 2.x writes its main report only as parquet. mzLib reads it into the same record as the 1.8/1.9 report.tsv, so it is a fifth quantifiable type: readers_read_results(), readers_read_records() and flashlfq_quantify() take it. readers_formats() lists 39 types, up from 38, and 5 offer the quantifiable view, up from 4; 19 still offer none. Like the TSV report it is recognised by its columns (Precursor.Id, Stripped.Sequence, Run), not its name, and any other .parquet is an mzlib_usage_error. Its retention_time_unit is "minutes", as for the TSV report. absent_fields is always empty for it, because there is no text header to judge from, so the columns 2.x stopped writing (File.Name, PG.Quantity, MS2.Scan and others) are NA in readers_read_records() without being named there, and ms2_scan_number reads 0.
  • peptidoform_convert(target = "ProForma") names UniProt modifications by UNIMOD accession (mzLib 1.0.594, #1403). [UniProt:N-acetylserine on S]SEQK becomes [UNIMOD:1]-SEQK, where it was written back by name; the caveat that said so is retired, so a result carries five caveats, not six. The pro_forma column readers_read_records() computes for a .psmtsv written without one gains the same accessions.

Every other result mzLib 1.0.594 and 1.0.595 changed, listed after the fact: pyMzLib measured each with the bridge at d10017ce, and the conversions, the stats_fit() prior and the entrapment_fraction column were re-checked from R against the pyMzLib 0.5.0 bridge. The help pages carry them too, rendered from the bridge’s specs.

Calls that used to succeed are now refused.

  • ProForma input that lost part of itself (mzLib #1462). peptidoform_convert(..., source = "ProForma") converted PEPTIDE-[UNIMOD:2][UNIMOD:35] with one C-terminal modification dropped, and read PEPTIDE-[UNIMOD:2]K as PEPTIDEK. Stacked terminal modifications now fail with failure_reason "IncompatibleModifications" (incompatible_items: “Multiple C-terminal modifications (2 found).”), and a residue after a C-terminal modification, a leading - or a modification with no sequence fail with "InvalidSequence".
  • SUMO remnants named ... on D (mzLib #1432). mzLib’s human SUMO-1 and SUMO-2/3 remnants (DVIEVYQEQTGG (SUMO-1 Site human), DVFQQQTGG (SUMO-2/3 Site human)) now target K, where they targeted D. A full sequence that names the on D form no longer converts; the on K form does.
  • TMTpro on S, T, Y or H (mzLib #1419). mzLib used to turn these into TMT, 224 Da, so PEPS[Common Fixed:TMTpro on S]K converted at the wrong mass. They now fail to convert. TMTpro on K is unchanged (+304.2071 Da).

Calls that used to fail now succeed.

  • flashlfq_quantify() with gapped replicate numbers (mzLib #1422). A design whose biological replicates skip a number, with fractions, raised an error; it now quantifies. So does the numbering the bridge uses when spectra gives no biological_replicate, which skips at every condition after the first. bayesian_protein_quant = TRUE on such a design now writes BayesianProteinQuant.tsv to output_directory.
  • A condition whose name ends in digits (mzLib #1424). Condition A1 biorep 0 beside condition A biorep 10 raised an mzlib_bridge_error in flashlfq_quantify() and flashlfq_median_polish(), because the two spell the same text. It now quantifies.

Same file, different value.

  • Entrapment and contaminant flags read every joined label (mzLib #1371). In readers_read_records() and readers_read_protein_groups(), is_decoy, is_contaminant and is_entrapment are TRUE when any |-joined parent is D, C or E. A protein group labelled T|C is now a contaminant and T|ET entrapment; on a .psmtsv the “E” in MetaMorpheus’s “Output too long for Excel” no longer reads as entrapment. Labels MetaMorpheus writes itself read as before.
  • readers_read_records() of a .psmtsv or .osmtsv gains an entrapment_fraction column (mzLib #1371): the share of each PSM that is an entrapment discovery, from 0 to 1. A shared T|ET counts half when the sequences differ and nothing when both proteins carry the same peptide. Use it, not is_entrapment, to count entrapment discoveries. It is NA where mzLib cannot line the label up with the full sequence (mzLib’s NaN).
  • Lactylation on K weighs one hydrogen more (mzLib #1417). mzLib’s formula is now C3H4O2, 72.021129 Da, where it was C3H3O2, 71.013304 Da. peptidoform_convert(..., target = "MassShift") of PEPK[Less Common:Lactylation on K]R gives PEPK[+72.021129]R, and the "ProForma" and "Unimod" targets write UNIMOD:2114. A .psmtsv’s pro_forma column changes the same way.
  • flashlfq_quantify(normalize = TRUE) (mzLib #1422). The reference is now the first condition’s lowest biological replicate, and each fraction’s lowest technical replicate, taken in numeric order. A design numbered from 1 is now normalized; before, biorep normalization did nothing for it. A gapless design numbered from 0 and listed in order is unchanged.
  • stats_fit() on fewer than 3 features (mzLib 1.0.594, #1398). mzLib fits no prior, as limma does: prior$df is 0, each feature keeps its own variance, and t and p are ordinary per-feature t-tests. They used to borrow a prior fitted to the two features. The 0.5.0 bridge still reports the first feature’s own variance as prior$scale there; bridges from pyMzLib 0.5.1 report NA, and each feature’s value is in the prior_variance column. ?stats_fit says both. Tables of 3 or more features are unchanged.
  • peptidoform_fragments() with a |P protease (mzLib #1320). protease = "trypsin|P" cut a protein that begins RP or KP after its first residue; it no longer does, and the other |P proteases change the same way. mzLib’s default "trypsin", and any protein that begins with M, are unaffected.
  • PRIDE: a failure that can pass is retried (mzLib 1.0.594, #1412). Every pride_ function retries such a failure three times, after 5, 20 and 60 seconds, so an outage takes longer to report. An FTP listing that comes back empty, which pride_list_ftp_files() used to return as no files (and so mzlib_project_not_found), is retried and then raised as an mzlib_bridge_error with error_type "HttpRequestException". A failed download leaves <name>.partial and <name>.partial.validator behind, so the next call resumes.
  • PRIDE downloads are not checked yet. mzLib can check a download against PRIDE’s checksums and catch an EBI error page served at the right size (#1427, #1449), but not on the path pride_download() and pride_download_files() use, so a file can be reported as downloaded when its bytes are wrong. ?pride_download and the PRIDE article say to check large files yourself.
  • ?stats_fit no longer says contrasts are not implemented: mzLib has them (EmpiricalBayes.ModerateContrasts, #1452), but stats_fit() does not expose them yet.
  • The psmtsv caveat on readers_read_results() cites SpectrumMatchFromTsv.cs:122 and :197; mzLib #1371 moved the lines it cited. The claim is unchanged.

mzLib 1.0.593

  • readers_read_protein_groups(), readers_read_quantified_peptides() and readers_read_occupancy() read an RNA search’s AllQuantifiedTranscriptGroups.tsv and AllQuantifiedOligos.tsv (mzLib #1388). mzLib reads them with subclasses of the protein-group and peptide readers, so the columns keep their protein names: protein_group_name is the transcript group, sequence the oligonucleotide, and occupancy names RNA modifications.
  • MetaMorpheus protein-group tables written without quantification now read (mzLib #1365): AllProteinGroups.tsv and each file’s <file>_ProteinGroups.tsv failed with Tsv file type not supported, and now read as MetaMorpheusQuantifiedProteinGroups, with intensity in absent_fields.
  • Four shipped modifications now write their Unimod accession in pro_forma (mzLib #1328): GG (Ubiquitination Site) as [UNIMOD:121], both Myristoylation entries as [UNIMOD:45] and EQIGG as [UNIMOD:846], instead of by name. Masses are unchanged.
  • A read fault on an existing .mzid is an mzlib_bridge_error naming the file (mzLib #1362), where it was an IOException. A missing file is still an mzlib_usage_error.
  • PRIDE download errors name the file and the host, never the URL (mzLib #1350), so a reviewer token in a query string cannot reach a log. They are still mzlib_service_unavailable.
  • The help pages no longer state how many file types mzLib recognises: readers_formats() asks mzLib, and a number written down goes stale at the next release.

Reading files

  • readers_formats() and readers_identify() say what a file is and which cross-format views it offers.
  • readers_read_spectra() reads scans from mzML, Thermo .raw, Bruker .d, timsTOF .d, MGF and msalign: headers always, peaks on request.
  • readers_read_results(), readers_read_features() and readers_read_matches() read the three cross-format views of search results; readers_read_records() reads any recognised file into that format’s own fields.
  • readers_retention_time_in_minutes() converts using each file’s declared unit, and refuses when there is none - for a _many batch, each file’s rows by that file’s unit.
  • Many files in one call: readers_identify_many() and a _many form of every reader hand the whole list to one bridge process with threads and on_error stated, and return one long records table plus a files data.frame of per-file facts, one row per input (needs the pyMzLib 0.2.0 bridge).
  • Every read reports the per-file block: reader, rows_not_read, retention_time_unit, caveats, and the three ways a column can be empty kept apart - absent_fields (the format has no source for it, so it is NA in every row), failed_fields and excluded_fields.
  • readers_read_spectra() reports the run’s source: instrument model and its PSI-MS accession, serial number, and acquisition start time with whether it is UTC (mzLib #1349).
  • readers_read_matches() reads mzIdentML (.mzid, .mzid.gz) with each match’s q_value, rank and pass_threshold, and with scores = TRUE one row per engine score; mzIdentML items mzLib does not represent are listed in skipped with the reason.
  • New readers_read_protein_groups(), readers_read_quantified_peptides() and readers_read_occupancy() read MetaMorpheus and FlashLFQ quantification tables long, one row per record per sample, and per-site PTM occupancy (mzLib #1347; needs the pyMzLib 0.2.0 bridge).
  • mzlibr_bridge_version() reports verbs, every command the bridge dispatches.
  • mzLib now recognises Pytheas, mzIdentML and its gzipped form, and the MetaMorpheus and FlashLFQ quantification tables.
  • limit = 0 is accepted by every reader, as the bridge allows: the envelope alone.

SDRF-Proteomics

  • sdrf_read() reads one experimental-design file and sdrf_pool() pools several into one analysis table with provenance; sdrf_value(), sdrf_all(), sdrf_records() and the other sdrf_ accessors read them.
  • sdrf_validate(), sdrf_lint(), sdrf_assess(), sdrf_samples() and sdrf_parse_ages() ask mzLib whether an SDRF document is well-formed, whether several agree on their vocabulary, whether it describes its samples, and what its ages are in years; sdrf_validate_many(), sdrf_assess_many() and sdrf_samples_many() read a corpus in one bridge call (mzLib #1207, #1325, #1326, #1333, #1335).
  • New sdrf_design() reads the label-free experimental design MetaMorpheus and FlashLFQ take out of an SDRF, with mzLib’s SdrfLabelFreeDesign, or every reason it refuses to - all at once, and as a result rather than an error. sdrf_design_spectra() and sdrf_design_run_design() hand it to flashlfq_quantify() and flashlfq_median_polish(); out writes MetaMorpheus’s ExperimentalDesign.tsv. Its replicate and fraction coordinates stay 0-based, as the quant functions take them (mzLib #1363; needs the pyMzLib 0.3.0 bridge).

Isobaric kits

  • New isobaric_kits() lists mzLib’s TMT, TMTpro, iTRAQ and DiLeu kits with every channel’s label, theoretical reporter-ion m/z and matching window, or one kit by MetaMorpheus’s name for it; channel_index is 1-based (mzLib #1375; needs the pyMzLib 0.3.0 bridge).

PRIDE, peptidoforms and quantification

  • pride_list_files(), pride_list_ftp_files(), pride_download() and pride_download_files() list and fetch PRIDE Archive projects.
  • pride_search() finds PRIDE projects by keyword, one row per project, with dates as Date.
  • peptidoform_fragments() digests a UniProt entry and fragments its peptidoforms.
  • New peptidoform_convert() rewrites full sequences in another notation with mzLib’s SequenceConversionService. The main use is MetaMorpheus full sequences to Unimod accessions: [UniProt:N-acetylserine on S]SEQK becomes [UNIMOD:1]SEQK, and dimethyllysine becomes UNIMOD:36. One row per input, in order, in records, with mzLib’s own verdict (converted, converted_with_warnings or failed), the modifications it could not write, and its warnings. source and target take any notation mzLib has registered; every result lists them. mode is mzLib’s SequenceConversionHandlingMode. The ProForma target names UniProt modifications by UNIMOD accession too, since mzLib #1403 (see mzLib 1.0.595 above; at mzLib 1.0.593 it wrote them back by name, mzLib#1401). (pyMzLib #75; needs the pyMzLib 0.4.0 bridge.)
  • flashlfq_quantify() runs FlashLFQ label-free quantification with match-between-runs.
  • flashlfq_median_polish() re-runs FlashLFQ’s protein median polish from a QuantifiedPeptides.tsv under a new experimental design, without re-reading spectra.
  • flashlfq_quantify() no longer warns about mzLib#1111 when max_threads is not 1: mzLib#1155 fixed it inside the pinned bridge. The default stays 1 here (pyMzLib and mzLibRust use -1).
  • flashlfq_median_polish() with no design no longer hangs in terminal R. A call that sends the bridge nothing on stdin now gives it an empty stdin rather than R’s own, which a terminal never closes. Every verb goes through the same transport, so none can wait on it (pyMzLib #73).

Differential abundance

  • New stats_fit() fits one linear model per feature of a feature-by-sample table and tests each named coefficient with limma’s empirical-Bayes moderated t, Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted: lmFit() then eBayes(legacy = TRUE), computed by mzLib’s LinearModel and EmpiricalBayes. A feature that cannot be fitted is reported with its reason, never dropped, and residual_df_differ says when default limma would use a different prior estimator.
  • New stats_adjust() Benjamini-Hochberg adjusts p-values from anywhere, keeping every position; NA is untested and not counted in m.
  • New stats_meta() pools one estimate per study into a DerSimonian-Laird random-effects estimate per feature, with direction agreement and leave-one-out sensitivity.
  • The tests hold all three to limma, metafor and stats::p.adjust() to 1e-8 relative - against their recorded output always, and against limma and metafor run in the test when they are installed (both are now in Suggests). The reference tables ship in extdata/stats/ so the examples and the new article read real files (mzLib #1341, #1357; needs the pyMzLib 0.3.0 bridge).

Protein databases

  • New proteins_read() reads UniProt XML or FASTA databases into one row per protein - organism, NCBI taxon, gene names, length, mass - with GO terms and Ensembl gene links on request; proteins_resolve_genes() resolves proteins to stable Ensembl gene ids against a gene set you pin; proteins_classify_peptides() calls each peptide Unique, SharedWithinGene, SharedAcrossGenes or NotInDatabase, with I and L one residue. One database or many, in one bridge call (mzLib #1336, #1338, #1348; needs the pyMzLib 0.2.0 bridge).
  • New proteins_annotate_go() annotates a stored MetaMorpheus protein-group table with Gene Ontology terms: one row per (group, term) that any member holds, directly or through an ancestor, naming the members that carry it, so consensus and direct-only views are filters on the rows. Every non-decoy group gets a row, a term-less one saying why. It reads the go.obo you name and never downloads one; proteins_update_go() is the one function that fetches the current release, keeping the previous file beside it (mzLib #1353, #1366; needs the pyMzLib 0.3.0 bridge).

Documentation

  • Every help page for a wire verb now carries that verb’s facts, generated from the bridge’s per-verb spec rather than retyped: what it wraps in mzLib, every parameter with its unit, range and default, every returned field and column with its unit and what NA means, the errors it raises as condition classes, caveats, the same verb in pyMzLib and mzLibRust, references and since. scripts/name-parity.R checks the hand-written @param and @return text against the same specs, and CI fails on any difference.
  • Every exported function has an example, and R CMD check runs them all: a stand-in bridge answers each call from a recording of the real one, so the examples need no bridge, .NET or network.
  • New ?mzlib_error documents the condition classes and how to handle each.
  • A pkgdown site, with an article for each module.
  • The articles are now vignettes, so R CMD check builds and runs every one of them, on every platform, against the replay bridge. Each opens with a question -> function -> mzLib table, ends with what to cite (rendered from the specs’ DOIs, each checked to resolve), and states no count of formats or verbs and no mzLib version in its prose; scripts/docs-lint.R holds all of that in CI.
  • The articles teach on real data recorded from the real bridge: a FlashLFQ run with match-between-runs on mzLib’s K562 pair (and median polish reproducing its protein intensities for every group), the whole albumin digest, PXD000001’s live FTP listing, an RNA search’s transcript groups, and the MALAT1 dilution series for stats_fit().
  • Corrected from those runs: the K562 peptide roll-up shows 21 of the 140 MBR transfers, not 52; use_pep_q_value filters nothing, it changes the q-value FlashLFQ carries; PXD000001’s FTP tree now holds 14 files.
  • knitr and rmarkdown join Suggests, for the vignettes. The package still imports nothing but base R.
